_comment: Safety baseline for autonomous Conductor runs in this work_dir. The Conductor opens SDK sessions with settingSources:['project'] and cwd=this directory, so the baseline in claude_code/DEV/full_stack_sm/.claude/settings.json is never seen from here. Without this file, runs had no deny list and no PreToolUse guard at all. CORRECTION (2026-08-26): this comment used to claim settings.local.json is loaded too, and the 'allow' rules were parked there on that assumption. It is NOT — settingSources:['project'] loads THIS file only; 'local' is a separate source the Conductor does not pass. So every allow rule in settings.local.json has been invisible to autonomous runs, and with permissionMode 'acceptEdits' only edits are auto-approved: Bash/WebSearch/WebFetch fell through to a permission prompt that a headless run cannot answer, i.e. a silent deny. That is why the ai-tells detector never ran on the 2026-08-25 article (blocked twice, in seo-editor Pass 3c and again in seo-publisher, and reported as a 'sandbox restriction') and why the shipped draft cites zero third-party sources. The allow list below is the autonomous-run set and must live HERE. Still deliberately no 'ask' array — a headless session cannot answer a prompt; irreversible actions are gated by the Conductor's ASK_PATTERNS over Telegram and by hooks/guard.py.

permissions._allow_comment: Scoped to what the pipelines actually shell out for: the ai-tells detector (referenced by seo-editor, social-editor, message-sequencer, brand-checker and the page-builder skill), the outbound registry, and the Ahrefs keyword pull that feeds seo-planner's keywords_raw. Deliberately NOT the broad 'Bash(python3:*)' that settings.local.json carries for interactive use: guard.py can only pattern-match a command STRING, so `python3 -c "..."` would sail past every rule in it. Narrow script rules keep arbitrary python out of autonomous runs while letting the reviewed scripts through. Both bare and ./-prefixed forms are listed because a blocked path variant fails the same silent way this fix exists to stop. WebSearch/WebFetch are needed for the writer's source-fetching; fetches are read-only and the deny list still blocks secret reads. Added 2026-09-01: the social pack mechanics (`social_pack.py` — profiles, source of record, run brief, the byte-identical drafter prompt, manifest, digest, report), the per-post mechanical gate (`post-lint.py`) and the LinkedIn brief splitter. These are the scripts that replaced ~165 ad-hoc Bash calls and the hand-written digest inside the coordinator's context; if any of them is silently denied the pipeline falls back to doing that work in an LLM again, which is the cost this change exists to remove. Both bare and ./-prefixed forms are listed for the same reason as the others. Added 2026-09-03: `content-plan-sync.py`, which pulls the strategy spreadsheet and reports drift against content-plan.{csv,md} and the inventory. seo-planner resolves every article against the offline copy at Phase 0, so a run that cannot check whether that copy is current plans against whatever priority the repo happened to freeze — which is exactly what happened on 2026-09-03, when the md was two months stale and two priorities had moved. Its default mode is read-only; only --sync writes, and it snapshots first.

_subagentPromptCacheTtl_comment: 1h, not the 5m default. Measured on the glp-1-market pack (2026-08-28): nine post-drafter runs paid 732K cache-creation tokens between them and shared nothing, because they started 4-6 minutes apart and the subagent cache TTL is 5 minutes. With `scripts/social_pack.py prompt` giving all nine a byte-identical ~7.1K-token prefix, an hour of TTL is what lets eight of them read that prefix instead of writing it. 1h cache writes are billed above the 5m rate, so this only pays while the prefix is actually shared — if the pack ever stops using the generated prompt, revisit this. Ignored while the subscription is in overage.
